notes:
Summary: Closed-lost to hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock). POC completed Jan 2026; Redwood met latency and throughput targets but lost on procurement friction and integration preference.

Key background and context:
- Company: Velaris ML Insights, large adtech platform running real-time bidding and ranking. Heavy AWS footprint (EKS, Kinesis, Redshift).
- Problem: Want low-latency ranking + embedding generation for bidding signals. Target: p50 <= 50ms, sustained 500 rps per region, burst to 2k rps. Cost sensitivity moderate but procurement prioritized operational simplicity.
- Initial interest: private/dedicated for isolation + audit controls. Provided pricing deck + security FAQ. SE ran POC (dedicated pool) in us-east-1.

POC / timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (Arjun) — discovery, high-level requirements captured. Fireflies id ff_20251120_101.
- 2025-12-08: Technical deep-dive with infra and security (Lena). Collected SSO/SAML and KMS requirements.
- 2025-12-20: POC kickoff — test dataset and perf baselines shared.
- 2026-01-10: POC mid-review — Redwood met p50 targets in us-east with dedicated pool; observed 5-8% higher per-token cost vs expected.
- 2026-01-18: Security questionnaire submitted (see drive:/security/velaris-soc2-answers.docx).
- 2026-01-22: Procurement signals delay; asks for AWS managed baseline pricing and integration plan.
- 2026-01-27: Final exec call — CTO comment: "we need something AWS-native to avoid procurement overhead and cloud governance friction." Decision to move to AWS Bedrock proof-of-concept.
- 2026-01-30: AE follow-up; procurement confirms preference for hyperscaler managed endpoints due to centralized vendor list and available enterprise credits.

Why we lost / root causes (short):
- Procurement bias to AWS-native solutions to avoid new vendor procurement and simplify risk review.
- Price delta vs hyperscaler managed endpoints once enterprise discounts/credits applied.
- No internal champion after initial ML lead promoted — momentum lost.
- Security team comfortable with AWS native service posture; additional audit evidence for Private deployment introduced delays.

What went well / signals to capture:
- Redwood met stated perf SLOs in the POC environment.
- SE feedback: integration hooks (prefix caching, KV reuse) worked as expected, positive feedback from infra on autoscaling behavior.
- Customer appreciated observability demo (token-level cost breakdown) — good marketing asset.

Next steps / playbook items (for Redwood ops):
- Archive as closed-lost but mark in CRM as "lost_to_hyperscaler" for product/market analysis.
- Capture pricing comparison and procurement language that led to decision; add AWS-managed pricing templates to competitive playbook.
- Ask for short post-mortem with procurement (one-pager) asking whether credits/marketplace listing would change outcome.

Open artifacts & references:
- Drive: drive:/decks/velaris-demo-v2.pptx (demo deck sent 2025-12-21).
- Drive: drive:/security/velaris-soc2-answers.docx (security questionnaire answers).
- Jira: JIRA-MLINF-3321 (POC infra incident: transient KV cache eviction).
- Fireflies: ff_20260112_7890 (final exec call).

Direct quote: CTO (email 2026-01-27) — "We appreciate Redwood's performance, but procurement will not onboard another inference vendor unless it's an AWS managed service. Simplifies compliance and billing."

Short next step for AE: send archived exec summary to growth@redwood and request one-pager from product about marketplace integrations.
